articles.title: Cardiovascular safety of orforglipron versus insulin glargine in adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk (ACHIEVE-4): a phase 3, event-driven, randomised, open-label, non-inferiority, active comparator trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Orforglipron is an oral, non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist. While some peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists have established cardiovascular benefit, the cardiovascular safety of non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists has not been studied. This study aimed to compare the effect of orforglipron with insulin glargine on the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in individuals with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight who are at increased risk for cardiovascular events. METHODS: This event-driven, phase 3, multicentre, randomised, open-label, active comparator, parallel-group study was conducted in 317 sites across 16 countries and territories. Adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk with glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) concentrations between 7·0% and 10·5% (53-91 mmol/mol) and a BMI of 25 kg/m2 or more, treated with up to three glucose-lowering medications (metformin, a sulfonylurea, and/or an SGLT2 inhibitor), were randomly assigned (1:1) to oral orforglipron maximum tolerated dose (up to 36 mg capsule [equivalent to 17·2 mg tablet]) or injectable titrated insulin glargine, each administered once daily. All participants had established cardiovascular or chronic kidney disease. The primary outcome was time to occurrence of four-component major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE-4), including cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for unstable angina. Non-inferiority of orforglipron to insulin glargine was declared if the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI for the hazard ratio (HR; orforglipron vs insulin glargine) was less than 1·8. The primary endpoint and other safety endpoints were assessed in all participants who took at least one dose of assigned treatment using all datapoints from baseline until withdrawal or study completion, regardless of treatment adherence. This trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05803421) and is completed. FINDINGS: Between May 1, 2023, and Sept 5, 2024, 2749 participants were randomly assigned (1371 to orforglipron and 1378 to insulin glargine). 1032 (38%) participants were female and 1717 (62·5%) male. 2362 (85·9%) participants had established cardiovascular disease and 1033 (37·6%) had chronic kidney disease. Mean baseline age, HbA1c, and BMI were 63·1 years (SD 9·9), 8·2% (1·0), and 33 kg/m2 (6·2), respectively. Over a median follow-up of 2 years, the primary outcome occurred in 57 (4·2%) of 1358 orforglipron participants and 67 (5·0%) of 1343 insulin glargine participants, showing non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4 (HR 0·84; 95% CI 0·59-1·20; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority). Gastrointestinal adverse events were reported in 851 (62·1%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 193 (14·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants; clinically significant or severe hypoglycaemia (glucose <3 mmol/L [54 mg/dL]) occurred in 93 (6·8%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 260 (19·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants. 62 deaths were reported during the study: 19 (1·4%) of 1371 participants receiving orforglipron and 43 (3·2%) of 1355 participants receiving insulin glargine; all deaths except one (in the insulin glargine group) were deemed unrelated to treatment. INTERPRETATION: In people with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk, the cardiovascular safety of orforglipron was confirmed by demonstrating non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent adverse event and most common reason for orforglipron treatment discontinuation with orforglipron, while clinically significant hypoglycaemia occurred less frequently with orforglipron than with insulin glargine. These findings support orforglipron as a potential once-daily, oral treatment option with established cardiovascular safety in people with type 2 diabetes and increased cardiovascular risk. FUNDING: Eli Lilly and Company.

articles.title: A phase 2 trial of daratumumab monotherapy for patients with newly diagnosed cardiac stage IIIb AL amyloidosis.
articles.abstract: Treatment options for patients with immunoglobulin light chain (AL) amyloidosis and advanced cardiac involvement remain limited. The prospective phase 2 European Myeloma Network 22 trial included patients with previously untreated AL amyloidosis, measurable hematologic disease, and Mayo2004/European cardiac stage IIIB disease to receive daratumumab monotherapy at the standard dose and schedule for up to 2 years (28-day cycles); patients with inadequate response after 3 cycles could additionally receive weekly bortezomib and dexamethasone. The primary end point was 6-month overall survival (OS) rate. Of 40 patients enrolled, 10 (25.0%) received additional treatment with bortezomib and dexamethasone. The 6-month OS rate was 65% (95% confidence interval, 48.2-77.6), and median OS was 10.4 months. The best hematologic response rate (partial response or better) up to 6 months was 75% (very good partial response or better, 47.5%; complete response, 12.5%), with the median time to first and best hematologic response being 1 week and 2.3 months, respectively. Cardiac response rate at 6 months was 30%. Common serious adverse events were cardiac failure (25%), sudden cardiac death (10%), and acute kidney injury (7.5%). The patients' quality of life remained stable throughout the trial treatment and observation. In patients with high-risk, advanced (stage IIIB) AL amyloidosis, daratumumab monotherapy was feasible and well tolerated, achieving rapid hematologic responses and associated with prolonged survival relative to historical cohorts. Cardiac response rates at 6 months were significant, considering advanced cardiac disease. These findings support daratumumab as the backbone of anticlonal therapy in advanced cardiac AL amyloidosis. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as #NCT04131309.

articles.title: Long-term Outcomes of Renal Function Following CTO PCI: Insights on Contrast Exposure.
articles.abstract: The impact of contrast volume on long-term renal outcomes after chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains uncertain, and the causal role of contrast exposure is increasingly questioned, particularly beyond the acute phase. The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between procedural contrast volume and long-term deterioration in renal function among patients undergoing CTO PCI. This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients undergoing CTO-PCI between 2019 to 2025 and had both baseline and ≥90-day follow-up creatinine measurements available. The main endpoint was persistent kidney dysfunction (≥25% decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)). Other relevant endpoints included Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) stage progression (≥1 stage), and rapid progression (≥2 stages). Contrast volume was analyzed as a continuous variable and by quartiles. Multivariable regression models and sensitivity analysis (using a ≥40%eGFR decline threshold and baseline chronic kidney disease) were performed. A total of 275 patients were included with a median follow-up of 3.3 years. Renal function significantly declined (median ΔeGFR: -17.0 ml/min/1.73 m²; p < 0.001). Persistent kidney dysfunction occurred in 52.4% of patients, KDIGO stage progression in 60.7% and rapid progression in 12.0%. Contrast volume (median 215 mL) was not independently associated with persistent kidney dysfunction (p = 0.267) and no dose-response relationship was observed across quartiles. Findings were consistent across models for ΔeGFR, KDIGO-based, subgroups and sensitivity analyses. Patient-related factors including age, male sex, hypertension, and diabetes emerged as independent predictors of renal decline. Notably, baseline renal function showed an inverse association with progression (p <0.001), suggesting a "ceiling effect" in advanced stages. In patients undergoing CTO-PCI, contrast volume is not independently associated with long-term renal deterioration. Persistent kidney dysfunction appears primarily driven by patient-related factors rather than procedural contrast exposure.

articles.title: Safety and complications of upper pole puncture in supine percutaneous nephrolithotomy.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Supine percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) has gained attention as a viable alternative to the traditional/historical prone approach for the treatment of large renal stones. However, concerns remain regarding the safety and feasibility of upper calyx punctures in the supine position, particularly for upper-pole access. This multicenter, retrospective cohort study evaluated the safety and stone-free rates of upper-pole punctures in supine PCNL, comparing outcomes with middle and lower calyx punctures and with literature on prone PCNL. METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed supine PCNL cases performed between 2009 and 2019 across eight international centers, categorizing patients by calyx of entry (upper, middle, or lower). Patients who required multiple calyx entries were excluded. Demographics, surgical details, and outcomes were recorded, including complications and stone-free rates. We used logistic regression to assess the association between stone-free rates and calyx puncture sites, adjusting for age, gender, Guy's Stone Score, and ASA score. Based on the initial findings, we performed a second multivariable logistic regression among patients undergoing upper calyx puncture using the same covariates. ANOVA was used to compare the means of quantitative variables, and Chi-square tests assessed associations between categorical variables. Bonferroni adjustment was applied when appropriate. RESULTS: Among 989 patients, 10% had upper, 28.5% middle, and 61.5% lower calyx punctures. No significant differences were found in overall complication rates when comparing upper, middle, and lower calyces. Thoracic complications were rare and did not differ significantly across calyces (p = 0.74). Upper calyx punctures had lower stone-free rates (51%) compared to middle (77.7%) and lower (62.8%) punctures (p < 0.001). The overall complication rate did not differ significantly (p = 0.82). According to the logistic regression, patients with a middle puncture site had 2.98 times higher odds of a stone-free outcome than those with an upper puncture site (OR, 2.98; 95% CI, 1.69-5.29). In contrast, patients with a lower puncture site did not have a significant difference in stone-free rates compared to those with an upper puncture (OR = 1.10, 95% CI: 0.64, 1.86, p = 0.7). Among patients undergoing upper calyx puncture, Guy's Stone Score 4 was independently associated with lower odds of achieving stone-free status (OR 0.20, 95% CI 0.04-0.91; p = 0.045). No significant associations were observed for age, gender, or ASA classification. CONCLUSION: Upper calyx punctures showed similar complication rates to middle and lower calyx punctures, with slightly lower stone-free rates likely due to higher stone complexity. These findings support the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of supine PCNL for upper calyx access.

articles.title: Association of Neutrophil Percentage-to-Albumin Ratio (NPAR) With Pathological Features and Long-Term Prognosis in Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Growing evidence highlights the central role of inflammation in the onset and progression of DKD. In this study, we investigate the association between the neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio (NPAR) and clinicopathological features, as well as long-term renal outcomes, in patients with diabetic kidney disease (DKD). Three hundred five biopsy-confirmed DKD patients with baseline eGFR ≥ 15 mL/min/1.73 m2 were retrospectively enrolled in this study. Baseline clinical and pathological characteristics were compared across NPAR quartiles. The primary outcome was 2-year DKD progression, defined as a > 40% increase in serum creatinine, end-stage renal disease, or all-cause mortality. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, and subgroup analyses were conducted to examine the association between the NPAR and kidney outcomes. Subsequently, a prognostic nomogram was constructed for DKD patients incorporating NPAR to stratify individual risk. Higher baseline NPAR quartiles were significantly associated with renal dysfunction and advanced renal pathological lesions. In a subset of renal biopsy specimens, MPO immunostaining demonstrated increased renal neutrophil infiltration in patients with higher NPAR quartiles. Renal MPO expression was positively correlated with mesangial expansion, interstitial fibrosis, and tubular atrophy. Among patients with complete follow-up, 65.3% developed the composite kidney outcome. Compared with the lowest NPAR quartile, multivariable-adjusted odds ratios (95% CIs) for kidney outcomes were 1.68 (0.36-8.15), 6.21 (1.35-33.55), and 6.88 (1.27-46.86) for Q2, Q3, and Q4, respectively. RCS analysis indicated a nonlinear association between NPAR and kidney outcomes, with risk increasing sharply above an NPAR value of 1.38. Subgroup analyses identified significant interactions between NPAR and Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodules as well as SGLT2 inhibitor use on kidney outcomes. A prognostic model incorporating NPAR quartiles, age, total cholesterol, eGFR, and interstitial fibrosis demonstrated good discrimination (AUROC 0.863). In conclusion, elevated NPAR is associated with increased renal neutrophil infiltration, more severe histopathological injury, and adverse renal outcomes in patients with DKD, and independently predicts long-term renal progression.
articles.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

articles.title: Comparative outcomes of arteriovenous accesses with and without tunneled hemodialysis catheters: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: This study compared patency rates of arteriovenous accesses with and without concurrent tunneled hemodialysis catheter (THC) use, addressing limited research on combined outcomes. A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted on patients undergoing arteriovenous access creation at a single hospital between January 2021 and December 2022. Primary outcomes were the 6-month primary patency rate and functional dialysis success. Secondary outcomes were the factors associated with each of these endpoints. Statistical analyses employed t tests, chi-square tests, logistic regression, and Kaplan-Meier survival curves. A total of 319 vascular accesses were included. The 6-month patency rate was significantly higher in the access-only group than in the access + THC group (87.04% vs 78.20%, P = .04). THC usage (odds ratio [OR] = 0.49, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.25-0.95, P = .03), graft usage (OR = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.18-0.82, P = .01), and higher hemoglobin levels (OR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.65-0.96, P = .02) were associated with reduced patency rates. Functional dialysis success at 6 months did not differ significantly between groups (87.96% vs 83.89%, P = .21). However, older age (OR = 0.96, 95% CI: 0.93-0.99, P = .01), use of a cubital artery to an autologous vein (OR = 0.39, 95% CI: 0.19-0.82, P = .01) or graft (OR = 0.40, 95% CI: 0.17-0.97, P = .04), and higher hemoglobin levels (OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.66-0.99, P = .03) were associated with a lower likelihood of functional dialysis success. Concurrent THC use was independently associated with reduced 6-month primary patency without a corresponding reduction in the short-term delivery of dialysis, suggesting an increased need for interventions to maintain the access. Judicious use of THCs and careful consideration of the vascular access type are important to optimize vascular access outcomes in patients undergoing hemodialysis.

articles.title: Effectiveness of a self-management intervention on clinical outcomes among patients with type 2 diabetes at high risk for Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a common complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and a leading cause of end-stage renal disease, posing substantial health and economic burdens. Early self-management interventions targeting modifiable risk factors are crucial to prevent or slow DKD progression. However, most studies focus on later stages of DKD, leaving a gap in early prevention for high risk of DKD individuals. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of a structured self-management intervention on clinical outcomes among T2DM patients at high risk of DKD. DESIGN: A prospective, two-arm, randomized controlled trial. SETTING: A tertiary hospital in Shandong Province, China. PARTICIPANTS: 134 patients with T2DM who were classified as being at high risk of DKD using a validated DKD risk prediction model. METHODS: 134 participants were randomized 1:1 to the intervention or control group. The intervention group received a 12-week a structured self-management program and 12-week follow-up. The control group received usual care. Clinical outcomes included hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), systolic blood pressure (SBP), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), body mass index (BMI), waist circumference (WC) were collected at baseline (T0), after the 12-week intervention (T1), and at 24 weeks (T2). Generalized estimating equations and intention-to-treat analyses were performed. Sensitivity analyses using multiple imputation were conducted. RESULTS: All participants completed the intervention phase. During the follow-up visits period, 7 participants in the intervention group and 9 participants in the control group were lost to follow-up at T1 (attrition rate: 11.94%), while 5 participants in the intervention group and 4 participants in the control group were lost to follow-up at T2 (attrition rate: 6.71%). No significant differences in baseline sociodemographic or clinical indicators between participants retained and those lost to follow-up (p > 0.05), suggesting data were missing at random. Baseline comparisons between the intervention and control groups revealed no significant differences in demographic or clinical indicators (p > 0.05). Compared with the control group, the intervention group demonstrated significant improvements in HbA1c, eGFR, SBP, and LDL-C, while no significant differences were observed for UACR, BMI, or WC. Sensitivity analyses yielded consistent results. CONCLUSIONS: The self-management intervention effectively improved HbA1c, eGFR, SBP and LDL-C among T2DM patients at high risk of DKD. These findings suggest that integrating structured self-management into routine diabetes care may help improve modifiable risk factors and support early DKD prevention. REGISTRATION: China Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400092745; registered on 22 November 2024).

articles.title: Acute kidney disease after acute kidney injury: incidence, risk factors, and association with
articles.abstract: Acute Kidney Disease (AKD) is defined as acute kidney injury (AKI) persisting for 7 to 90 days and represents a window for interventions to improve renal outcomes. However, data on AKD remain underexplored. This retrospective cohort study at Tongji Hospital, China, included 23,868 adult patients who survived at least one AKI episode between January 2015 and April 2024. Using electronic medical record data, we aimed to quantify the incidence of AKD among AKI survivors, identify independent risk factors, and evaluate the association between AKD and de novo chronic kidney disease (CKD). Among the cohort, 10,884 patients (45.6%) progressed to AKD. Multivariable logistic regression revealed that advanced age, preexisting hypertension, heart failure, cirrhosis, recent diuretic use, hepatorenal syndrome, higher baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate, higher AKI stage, and dialysis-requiring AKI were independent risk factors for AKD. Fine-Gray competing-risk analysis accounting for acute-phase mortality confirmed that higher AKI severity was independently associated with AKD progression. In a subcohort of 6597 patients without preexisting CKD who had at least one year of follow-up, 19.8% developed de novo CKD. Cox proportional hazards analysis demonstrated that patients with AKD had a significantly increased risk of de novo CKD compared to those without AKD (HR 1.92, 95% CI 1.70-2.17). These findings highlight the high proportion of AKD among patients with AKI, and emphasize the importance of early detection and targeted management for high-risk groups. It is critical to strengthen post-discharge renal function monitoring and intervention strategies for AKI patients to improve long-term renal outcomes.

articles.title: [Correlation between acute kidney injury diagnosed by serum creatinine and urine output criteria and short-term prognosis in critically ill patients following non-cardiac surgery].
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the correlation between acute kidney injury (AKI) diagnosed by elevated serum creatinine (Scr) versus only meeting the urine output (UO) reduction criteria and short-term adverse outcomes in critically ill patients following non-cardiac surgery, and to evaluate the association between even mild elevations in Scr and clinical outcomes furthermore. METHODS: This study was a secondary analysis of data from a prospective cohort study. A total of 1020 non-cardiac surgery adults admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) of Peking University First Hospital from May 20, 2019 to March 7, 2022 were included. According to Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guideline, AKI patients were classified into two groups: the AKI-Scr group (those meeting the Scr elevation criteria) and the AKI-UO group (those fulfilling only the UO reduction criteria). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality in patients with AKI, and the secondary outcomes were major renal adverse events, post-operative renal replacement therapy (RRT), postoperative complications, postoperative mechanical ventilation time, ICU stay, postoperative hospital stay, total hospital stay, and total medical costs. Multivariate Logistic regression analysis was used to identify risk factors of hospitalized death in critically ill patients with AKI following non-cardiac surgery. RESULTS: A total of 1020 non-cardiac surgical patients admitted to the ICU were enrolled, among whom 429 were diagnosed with AKI. There were 91 cases in the AKI-Scr group and 338 cases in the AKI-UO group. The primary study endpoint: no statistically significant difference in in-hospital mortality was observed between the AKI-Scr and AKI-UO groups (5.5% vs. 2.1%, P>0.05). The secondary study endpoints: compared with the AKI-UO group, the patients in the AKI-Scr group had a higher incidence of major renal adverse events (9.8% vs. 4.4%), postoperative RRT (4.4% vs. 0.3%) and postoperative complications (50.5% vs. 24.0%, all P < 0.05), a significantly longer duration of postoperative mechanical ventilation (12.0 d vs. 7.5 d), ICU stay (2 d vs. 1 d), postoperative hospital stay (14 d vs. 9 d) and total hospital stay (21 d vs.17 d, all P < 0.05), and a significantly higher total medical expenditure (112000 yuan vs. 89000 yuan, P<0.001). Multivariate Logistic regression analysis showed that postoperative RRT (OR=33.164, 95%CI: 1.305-842.794, P=0.034) and sepsis during hospitalization (OR=23.096, 95%CI: 4.242-125.175, P < 0.001) were independent risk factors for hospitalized death in the critically ill patients with postoperative AKI. Compared with the ΔScr≤24% patients (Scr increased by less than 24% from baseline within 7 d), even in the patients with only a minor elevation in Scr (ΔScr increase of 25%-49% from baseline but < 26.5μmol/L), the incidence of postoperative complications was significantly higher (48.6% vs. 19.2%, P < 0.001), along with prolonged ICU stay [1(1, 3) d vs. 1(1, 2) d], postoperative hospital stay (13 d vs. 9 d), and total hospital stay (23 d vs. 16 d, all P < 0.05). Compared with the non-AKI group, the incidence of in-hospital mortality (2.1% vs. 0.3%, P < 0.05) and postoperative complications (24.0% vs. 18.3%, P < 0.05) was higher in the AKI-UO group, and the ICU stay [1(1, 3) d vs. 1(1, 2) d, P < 0.001] was longer. CONCLUSION: In critically ill patients with AKI following non-cardiac surgery, the short-term prognosis of patients with AKI whose diagnosis was mainly based on increased Scr was worse than patients who only met the diagnostic criteria of oliguria. Even a mild elevation in serum creatinine was associated with adverse patient outcomes.
articles.journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences

articles.title: Association of baseline non-severe anemia with clinical outcomes following the first recorded diagnosis of systemic sclerosis: A matched cohort study.
articles.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) carries the highest mortality among systemic autoimmune diseases, yet the prognostic significance of anemia around the time of the first recorded SSc diagnosis is unclear. We examined whether baseline anemia is associated with early mortality and complications. This retrospective matched cohort study identified female adults with a first recorded SSc diagnosis between January 2010 and December 2024 from the TriNetX Research Network. Patients were required to have at least 5 years of pre-index observation without a documented SSc diagnosis. The network comprised 140 healthcare organizations, with approximately 70% of patients in the United States across all 9 census regions and 30% at international sites. Anemia was defined as hemoglobin (Hb) ≥8.0 and <12.0 g/dL and non-anemia as ≥12.0 g/dL, measured within ±30 days of diagnosis. For the Hb-stratified analysis, the anemia cohort was categorized as Hb ≥10.0 to <12.0 g/dL or ≥8.0 to <10.0 g/dL. One-to-one propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics, and Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The primary outcome was all-cause mortality during days 31 to 365 among patients surviving the 30-day landmark period; secondary outcomes were sepsis, acute kidney injury, intensive care unit admission, pulmonary fibrosis, and elevated C-reactive protein (≥10 mg/L). After matching, 5410 patients remained in each cohort. Baseline anemia was significantly associated with higher 1-year mortality (HR, 2.54; 95% CI, 1.99-3.22; P < .001) and with increased risks of sepsis (HR, 3.20; 95% CI, 2.38-4.30), acute kidney injury (HR, 2.24; 95% CI, 1.80-2.78), intensive care unit admission (HR, 1.92; 95% CI, 1.47-2.51), and elevated C-reactive protein (HR, 1.55; 95% CI, 1.37-1.74; all P < .001); no significant association was observed for pulmonary fibrosis (HR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.96-1.17; P = .229). Associations persisted in sensitivity analyses and over 3-year follow-up. Mortality risk showed a graded pattern across Hb strata (Hb ≥10.0-<12.0 g/dL: HR, 1.66; Hb ≥8.0-<10.0 g/dL: HR, 3.33). Baseline anemia was associated with increased mortality and acute systemic complications following the first recorded SSc diagnosis; these observational findings warrant prospective validation.

articles.title: Sustained potassium control and recurrent hyperkalemia during individualized potassium-guided sodium zirconium cyclosilicate titration in maintenance hemodialysis: a post hoc analysis of a randomized trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: A mean predialysis potassium value at a single visit does not show whether the same patient remains controlled across consecutive months or repeatedly crosses hyperkalemic thresholds. We evaluated sustained patient-level potassium control and recurrent hyperkalemia during individualized potassium-guided sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) therapy on non-dialysis days. METHODS: This exploratory post hoc analysis used data from a previously reported single-center, open-label randomized trial of 116 patients with chronic hyperkalemia (58 per group). The primary outcome was sustained response during months 3-6, which required all four scheduled predialysis potassium measurements after the long interdialytic interval to be available, at least three of the four values to be within 4.0-5.0 mmol/L, and no unplanned hemodialysis triggered by potassium ≥ 6.5 mmol/L during the evaluation period. Missing measurements were classified as nonresponse. Adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) were estimated using modified Poisson regression with robust standard errors. RESULTS: The primary outcome occurred in 25/58 (43.1%) SZC-treated participants and 8/58 (13.8%) controls (aRR 3.02, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.49-6.14). Sustained response within 4.0-5.5 mmol/L occurred in 38/58 (65.5%) and 22/58 (37.9%), respectively (aRR 1.74, 95% CI 1.19-2.54). At least two scheduled potassium values ≥ 5.5 mmol/L occurred in 11/58 (19.0%) and 36/58 (62.1%) (aRR 0.31, 95% CI 0.18-0.55). The adjusted incidence rate ratio for visits with potassium ≥ 5.5 mmol/L was 0.36 (95% CI 0.24-0.54). Complete-case and conservative extreme-case missing-data analyses were directionally consistent with the main analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Individualized potassium-guided SZC therapy was associated with a higher probability of meeting the sustained biochemical potassium-control criterion at scheduled monthly measurements and with fewer recurrent biochemical hyperkalemic excursions. Clinical outcomes were not evaluated in the present analysis; therefore, the observed biochemical improvements should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical benefit. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2600119050. Registered on 14 February 2026; retrospectively registered.

articles.title: Effect of uric acid and estimated glomerular filtration rate on the Fibrosis-4 index: A cross-sectional and cohort analysis.
articles.abstract: Hepatic steatosis and fibrosis present a significant public health burden, especially in China. Emerging evidence suggests an association between liver fibrosis and kidney function, indicating a potential relationship among uric acid (UA) levels, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index. This retrospective cohort study investigates the correlation between UA, estimated GFR, and FIB-4 index in Chinese adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) using cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses. A total of 5051 adults with MASLD were included from 8857 individuals initially screened at the International Healthcare Center, Fourth Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine. The main outcome measure was the FIB-4 index. Among the 5051 participants (75.4% male; mean age, 42.3 years), the mean baseline eGFR was 98.7 mL/min/1.73 m2. Participants with lower eGFR had significantly older age and higher body mass index, systolic blood pressure, triglycerides, UA levels, and FIB-4 index than those with higher eGFR (P < .001 for all). In multivariable Cox regression analyses, each 1-standard deviation decrease in eGFR was associated with a 21% higher risk of an increased FIB-4 index (hazard ratio [HR], 1.21; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.14-1.29; P < .001). Hyperuricemia (UA ≥ 420 μmol/L) was independently associated with a 38% higher risk of elevated FIB-4 (HR, 1.38; 95% CI: 1.23-1.55; P < .001). In the unadjusted model, a significant nonlinear dose-response relationship was observed between eGFR and FIB-4 (P for nonlinear trend < .001). However, after progressive adjustment for demographic variables, family history, and metabolic covariates, the nonlinear signal was markedly attenuated. Mediation analysis demonstrated that UA partially mediated the association between eGFR and FIB-4, accounting for 6.88% of the total effect. Reduced eGFR and hyperuricemia were independently associated with an elevated FIB-4 index in adults with MASLD, with a nonlinear relationship indicating a greater liver fibrosis risk in individuals with moderate to severe renal impairment (eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2). Partial mediation by UA suggests that metabolic dysregulation contributes to the kidney-liver interaction. Routine assessment of eGFR and UA may improve liver fibrosis risk stratification in patients with MASLD.

articles.title: Persistent hyperparathyroidism and its predictive factors in end-stage renal disease patients after kidney transplantation: A prospective study.
articles.abstract: Hyperparathyroidism (HPT) may persist in patients after kidney transplantation (KT). A better understanding of which patients are likely to have persistent HPT after KT would help in the development of optimal management strategies. Our aim was to examine the prevalence of persistent HPT after KT in a contemporary cohort and to identify risk factors associated with persistent HPT at 6 months. We followed 104 KT subjects in a longitudinal prospective cohort at Cho Ray Hospital, Vietnam, from October 2023 to May 2025. Persistent HPT was defined as a parathyroid hormone (PTH) level of 150 pg/mL at 6 months after KT. Among the 104 patients, the prevalence of persistent HPT at 6 months was 58.65%. The average PTH levels pretransplant and at 6 months posttransplant were 375.70 (IQR = 259.00-603.25) pg/mL and 167.95 (IQR = 112.53-227.30) pg/mL, respectively. Patients with persistent HPT had significantly higher baseline PTH (median 489 vs 273, P < .001) and alkaline phosphatase levels (median 102.0 vs 89.5, P = .025), and also experienced longer durations of chronic kidney disease (median 5.0 vs 2.0, P = .007) and dialysis therapy (2.0 vs 1.0, P < .001). Higher pretransplant intact PTH was independently associated with persistent HPT across both multivariable models, whereas the association with dialysis duration was significant only when categorized as ≥1 year. Our findings suggest that high pretransplant intact PTH independently predicts persistent HPT at 6 months, whereas dialysis duration is only significant when it reaches 1 year or longer.
